newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA FIN MIN SETS ASIDE $135.1 MLN BRADY COUPON.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA FIN MIN SETS ASIDE $135.1 MLN BRADY COUPON.

text.p: Bulgaria's outgoing Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said on Wednesday that the ministry has received $135.1 million from the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development (SFRD) which will be transferred for Brady bond coupon payments due on January 28.
"The money was transferred from the SFRD to a finance ministry account to enable the payment," Kostov told Reuters.

Bulgaria issued on July 28, 1994 three types of Brady bonds with a total par value of $5.1 billion as part of a restructuring deal on its $8.16 billion commercial debt to the London Club of creditor banks.
The interest on the bonds is due on January 28 and July 28 each year and is transfered to the debt agent Citibank of Citicorp which distributes the payment to Bond holders.

Crisis-ridden Bulgaria's foreign exchange reserves stood at $518 million in December. The central bank has cautiously supported the collapsing lev which slid to 810 to the dollar from 650 in the beginning of the month and 70 a year ago.

A political and economic deadlock caused by the opposition's demands for early elections and firm insistence of the ruling ex-communists to form a second government has deterred vital talks with multilateral lenders on further reform and funding talks.
President Petar Stoyanov, who formally took office on Wednesday backed the opposition's calls for early elections. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
